page: Microsoft Azure D48s_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features an Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor operating at a nominal base frequency of 2.6 GHz. It provides 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with two threads per core, supported by a 35 MB L3 cache. System memory totals 192.0 GB of RAM, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include local disk storage or dedicated GPU hardware, requiring attached remote block storage such as Azure Premium Storage for persistent file systems.

Benchmark metrics place the D48s_v4 within the average tier across most compute, memory, and database evaluation tests. It recorded a Geekbench multi-core score of 12037.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 37944.73. Memory throughput demonstrates notable write capability, registering 94.85 GB/sec in large-block uncached write tests, which ranks in the upper quartile, while uncached read performance reaches 181.84 GB/sec. Due to the lack of hardware acceleration, large language model text generation throughput is constrained, registering 8.17 tokens/sec on 7B models and 57.23 tokens/sec on 135M models.

The instance offers balanced resource allocation across high vCPU density and memory capacity. Without bundled local storage, persistent I/O performance relies on external storage configuration. D48s_v4 is appropriate for scalable multi-threaded enterprise software, mid-tier relational and in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, web serving clusters, and batch data processing workloads that do not demand specialized GPU compute or ephemeral local NVMe performance.
description: Microsoft Azure D48s_v4 is a general-purpose instance featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs and 192.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. With 24 physical cores and hyper-threading enabled, the instance maintains a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It lacks bundled local storage and discrete GPUs, relying on remote block storage options such as Azure Premium Storage. In benchmark testing, the D48s_v4 demonstrates solid general computing performance, scoring 37944.73 in PassMark CPU and displaying strong large-block memory write throughput of 94.85 GB/sec. Application tests show 41.3 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and 29.92 GB/sec in static web throughput. Without GPU acceleration, text generation workloads remain resource-limited. The D48s_v4 provides a reliable profile for enterprise web applications, intermediate relational database servers, Redis caching infrastructure, and multi-threaded compilation or batch processing tasks.
